A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same transformer brain encoder and NSD experiments. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including relocated supplementary analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original fMRI prediction experiments across four subjects and multiple backbones, plus attention, query-similarity, and image-generation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds baseline comparisons, training-size experiments, and quantitative attention-selectivity results.

M1.justification: The frozen backbones, learned ROI or vertex queries, cross-attention decoder, masked linear readouts, MSE training, and layer ensembling are retained. The added pooling methods are comparison baselines, not revisions to the proposed encoder.

E1.justification: Both versions use NSD natural-image responses from subjects 1, 2, 5, and 7, including the existing caption-input and generated-image analyses. The training-size sweep and category analysis reuse this coverage without adding datasets, populations, or input scenarios.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds CLS + regression, PCA + regression, and DeepGaze-based saliency integration to the DINOv2 comparison. These substantially broaden the controls for dimensionality reduction and spatial pooling. The comparator sets in the retained ResNet50, CLIP, and BERT comparisons are unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols test training sizes of 550, 1100, 2200, 4400, and 8800 images (Table 2) and quantify categories among the top 2000 attention pixels after resizing maps to 434 × 434 and applying YOLO-derived labels (A.2). The original split, ten-fold prediction averaging, and encoding-accuracy metric remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial analyses of training-data requirements and quantitative category selectivity of attention maps across four subjects. These supplement v1's qualitative attention examples. Existing routing-granularity, layer-ensemble, query-similarity, and BrainDiVE analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten-fold prediction averaging and query-similarity averages across 20 models using five seeds and four backbone layers. Neither adds confidence intervals or significance tests. The new checklist explains separate subject reporting without changing the statistical practice.

E6.justification: Matched encoding scores from v1 Tables 1–5 remain unchanged in v2 Tables 1 and 3–6. Substantial new results include the added baseline scores, training-size curves in tabular form, and attention-category proportions. For example, the new DINOv2 Subject 1 scores are 0.38 for CLS regression, 0.52 for PCA regression, and 0.38 for saliency integration.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theoretical results or proofs. The mathematical substance of the attention mechanism, regression, and ensembling descriptions is unchanged; the new attention-category summaries are empirical analyses.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the claims of accurate, parameter-efficient brain prediction, interpretable attention routing, and a plausible mechanistic account of high-level visual processing. The revised abstract does not materially redefine their scope.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new baselines through ROI-specific versus generic pooling, argues applicability to smaller experiments from Table 2, and connects routing to content-dependent receptive-field shifts in the discussion. The NSD-only and anatomical-modeling limitations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix B identifies NVIDIA L40s cluster resources, approximately 3 TB storage, and aggregate estimates of 4000 training GPU hours plus 1000 for other experiments. New baseline implementations are described. Conversely, v1's explicit best-validation model-selection statement for each fold is omitted. Code-access information remains equivalent.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting saliency-based encoding, detection tools, neural attention, and receptive-field modulation, including Khosla et al., DeepGaze, Gilbert and Li, and Ramalingam et al. The principal positioning relative to factorized readouts, self-supervised backbones, and DETR remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and selected passages receive language edits and explanatory additions, while the main section sequence remains intact. v2 adds acknowledgments, a compute section, and a NeurIPS checklist; inserting A.2 renumbers the retained query-similarity and image-generation sections.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains baseline rows, and v2 adds the training-size table and four attention-category tables. All original figures are retained. Other changes involve front-matter formatting, limited caption clarification, and reflow or relocation of existing displays, with their visual designs preserved.

improvement.justification: The added pooling controls, training-size evidence, quantitative attention summaries, and compute disclosure usefully strengthen the existing paper. The gain is limited by incomplete interpretation of the new evidence: A.2's broad category-selectivity summary leaves exceptions unexplained, such as Subject 5 RSC having 0.50 body versus 0.08 background pixels in Table 9.
